answer: Nectar River Routing.** Each agent's messages must traverse a randomly drawn path of established peers, and only nodes lying on many distinct paths accumulate routing credit (nectar) that unlocks outbound bandwidth. A cluster of fresh sybils forms a hollow in this topology: their internal paths never intersect the broader river of organic traffic, so they earn near-zero credit. To fake centrality, an attacker must rent real connections from many independent existing agents, paying per-link fees across dozens of unrelated operators—cost scaling with path diversity, not headcount.
